info.title: Telleo API
info.description: Start AI phone calls from your own systems and get each call's outcome back.

post.description:
Queues a call to one number and dials it as soon as a line is free and calling hours allow. Returns the call at once (usually `queued` or `dialing`); the outcome arrives on your webhook, or poll `GET /calls/{id}`.

Scope: `calls:write`.

200.description: Replay: a call with this `Idempotency-Key` already exists and is returned unchanged (`idempotent_replay: true`).

error.message: phone_number must be in E.164 format, e.g. +919876543210.

error.message: This account is out of AI calling credits. Top up to place calls.

No agent 17ea33d2-… in this account. List your agents with GET /v1/agents.

Agent 17ea33d2-… only answers incoming calls.

error.message: Too many requests. Retry after 12 seconds.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Any unique string per attempt, e.g. `lead-8812-1`. Retrying with the same key and the same body returns the first call instead of calling twice; a different body is refused (409). Honoured for 24 hours.

post.description:
Queues up to 1,000 calls in one request. Each row is checked on its own: valid rows are queued, invalid rows come back in `rejected` with the row's `index`. Batch calls are dialled as lines free up, behind single calls.

Scope: `calls:write`.

post.description: Sent once when a call ends without connecting: `no_answer`, `busy`, `failed`, `canceled` or `expired` (see `data.status` and `data.status_reason`).

ApiKey.name: X-API-Key
ApiKey.description: Your AI calling API key (`vak_call_…`). `Authorization: Bearer <key>` also works.

RequestId.description: Unique id of this request. Quote it to support.

code.description: Machine-readable code. Branch on this, not on the message.

message.description: A sentence you can log or show to an operator.

request_id.description: Quote this when you contact support.

details.description: Extra context, e.g. `errors: [{field, message}]` for validation errors or `call_id` for conflicts.

name.description: How the agent addresses the person. Fills `{{name}}` in the agent's script.

external_id.description: Your own id for this person or lead (CRM record id). Echoed back and filterable on `GET /calls`.

agent_id.description: The agent that makes the call. Required on `POST /calls`; on a batch row it overrides the batch's `agent_id`. List yours with `GET /agents`.

phone_number.description: E.164, e.g. `+919876543210`. Spaces, dashes, dots and brackets are ignored; a leading `00` is read as `+`.

variables.description: Values for the `{{placeholders}}` in the agent's script. Keys: a letter, then letters, digits, `_` or spaces, at most 40 characters. Values: text, number or boolean, at most 500 characters.

metadata.description: Anything you want back on the call and its webhook (at most 8 KB as JSON). The agent never sees it.

test.description: Simulate the call: no phone rings and nothing is billed. It completes at once with a sample outcome and fires your webhook.

Outcome.description: What the AI took from the conversation. `null` until it has been processed (usually within a minute of the call ending), and for calls that did not connect.

call_quality.description: `failed` when the call broke down on our side; then `disposition` is `Incomplete` and `lead_rating` is null. Call the contact again rather than changing their stage.

disposition.description: The agent's label for how the call went, from the dispositions configured on the agent (e.g. Interested, Not interested, Call back later).

answers.description: Each of the agent's extraction questions and the answer given.

lead_rating.description: The AI's 1–10 score of the contact's interest; `null` when it could not tell.

callback_time_text.description: When the contact asked to be called back, in their words (e.g. `tomorrow after 6 pm`).

follow_up.description: Whether a person should call this contact: `CALL` (now), `CALL_LATER` or `SKIP`. `null` when not assessed; never read `null` as `CALL`.

follow_up_note.description: One sentence on why, for the person deciding whether to call (at most 240 characters).

meeting.description: A meeting, demo, visit or callback the contact AGREED to at a specific day or time. `requested` is false when no time was agreed.

at.description: ISO-8601 with offset, resolved from what was said, e.g. `2026-10-14T18:00:00+05:30`.

time_text.description: The contact's own words, e.g. `tomorrow 6 pm`.

status_reason.description: Why a call is waiting or did not happen, in plain words. Present only when there is one.

scheduled_for.description: Present while a queued call is held until a later time (outside calling hours, a recall gap, the daily limit).

recording_url.description: A temporary link to the recording. Fetch the call again for a fresh link after `recording_expires_at`.

cost.description: What the call cost, once it has ended. `null` while it is still running.

credits.description: Credits charged. 0 for test calls and calls that did not connect.

billed.description: false for a few minutes after a connected call ends, until the charge is made.

idempotent_replay.description: Only on `POST /calls`: `true` when this is the call created by an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

call_id.description: For `call_already_queued`: the call already waiting for this number.

uses_contact_name.description: The script says the contact's name: send `contact.name`.

variables.description: Placeholders the script uses that you should send in `variables`.

can_place_calls.description: false when new real calls would be refused with 402.

calls_waiting.description: Calls queued and not yet dialled (API and dashboard).

calls_not_yet_billed.description: Connected calls whose charge has not been made yet.

secret.description: The signing secret. Returned only when the endpoint is first set and when the secret is rotated. Store it.

secret_hint.description: First and last characters of the secret, on reads.

id.description: Same on every retry of this event. Use it to ignore duplicates.
